demo_answers: You are having pernicious anemia. It is due to deficiency of vitamin B-12. Vitamin B-12 is required for normal functioning of red blood cells. So it causes anemia. Treatment is oral or intramuscular injections of vitamin B-12.

I am sorry to hear about your husbands' experience with his appendix surgery. It is true that some patients can have very long healing times after their surgeries. However, there are many factors that affect how quickly someone heals after surgery. These include age, weight, general health, nutrition, medications, smoking status, etc. In addition, if the patient has a history of poor wound healing, they may be at risk for having longer healing times.

As per your query you have symptoms of pain in jaw while chewing which can be due to temporomandibular joint disorder. Need not worry. I would suggest you to visit an oral physician once and get evaluated. Doctor may order x-ray of jaw and take impression of teeth. Doctor may prescribe muscle relaxant like chlorzoxazone along with analgesics like ibuprofen. Doctor may also refer you to physiotherapist for further treatment. Doctor may also recommend splint to wear at night.

You are having burning sensation while passing urine. It can be due to infection of urinary tract. You should go for routine hologram, random blood sugar, urine routine and microscopy examination. If needed you should go for culture and sensitivity test. You should take complete course of antibiotics as prescribed by your doctor.

You are having alcoholic hepatitis. It can be due to alcohol intake or other causes like viral infection. You should go for complete blood count, liver function test, viral markers, ultrasound abdomen. Then you should take treatment accordingly.

Your report suggests that you have high cholesterol level. You should take low fat diet, avoid saturated fats like butter, ghee, meat etc. Take more of fruits and vegetables in your diet. Avoid smoking and alcohol if any. Regular exercise will be helpful. Consult your doctor for further management.

You are having irregular menses. It can be due to hormonal imbalance or some other cause. I would suggest you to consult a gynecologist and get evaluated. If needed go for hormone replacement therapy.

PFO is a small hole between two chambers of heart. It is present in all people but it is usually closed by blood clots. In your case there is no clot formation so the hole remains open. This can cause problems like stroke, pulmonary embolism etc. So you should definitely get operated. There are many ways to close the hole. You can discuss with your doctor about it.
